newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee council to be installed January 17.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee council to be installed January 17.

text.p: A new Brazilian council to decide the country's internal and international coffee policy will to be installed on January 17 in Brasilia, private sector coffee officials said.

The council, Conselho Deliberativo da Politica Cafeeira (CDPC) or the Deliberative Council for Coffee Policy, is made up of private and public sector representatives. Its president is Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.

Dornelles will meet with each entity of the private sector individually before the committee is officially installed at 1200 local/1400 GMT, said David Nahum, secretary-general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association which represents roasters.

It is not yet known if the council will meet that day to decide a position ahead of an emergency council of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), to be held in Rio de Janeiro on January 23, Nahum said.
The ACPC council was called after the Ivory Coast and Colombia said they believed exports as agreed by ACPC members between January and June this year should be cut further.
The ACPC council will follow a three-day coffee seminar also to be held in Rio de Janeiro.

Private sector representatives of the CDPC will meet tomorrow at the headquarters of the National Coffee Council (CNC) in Sao Paulo to prepare for the new council, said CNC executive secretary Hercilio Amaral.
((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
